doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Stones mistakes, rehearsals and last-minute set lists
summary: The band rehearses many songs for weeks, set lists arrive just before the show and vary by city, with Chuck Leavell as musical director.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do the Rolling Stones, the core group, do they ever mess up in a concert?

I mean I would — I think they would say yeah but so what — I think that their mess-ups or their little things that happen that are like you know slightly different, they’re okay with that. You know for instance I remember once Keith — Keith has many guitars and he’s got a guitar tech that tunes like for almost every tune has a new guitar because it’s a different tuning. Like not every tune is — so this tune will be that. I remember once he got a guitar and put it on and either he went to the next song or it was the wrong guitar but he went and played the chord and it was like the wrong thing and Mick was like, “It’s the wrong chord, Mate” or something. You know it was just like — but then it was just laughable. It was like okay give me this guitar and then say — but you know those things happen. I mean they’re human you know? But I must say before we play the concerts we rehearse for a number of weeks and we’ve rehearsed let’s say 90 of their songs, then down to 70 then down to 60, then by the time the tour starts let’s say we have 40 songs ready to go out and every night we play like 20, 21, 22 songs. And they’ll introduce, you know, maybe of the 21 songs maybe 16 or 15 are always there and then they’ll intersperse like you know different ballad or a different this or different that. So then we put in those ones that we’ve rehearsed. In this city we’ll do that song or something like that. So they’re prepared in a sense, I mean they’re really ready. And of course the lighting and the staging and the you know everything set. They have this great, you know, oh this tune has that light and this — and everything’s like — it’s a show. It’s like a major production with hundreds of people that are traveling with us you know getting things prepared. The sound person and the back line people. It’s a massive like undertaking. So they’re as together as they can be. Any of the mistakes are more looked at as just part of life.
Do they ever make game time decisions like change their mind about a song list — “Let’s insert this now?”

Well we don’t get the song list until like right before the show. So like day of the show will be kind of like — show’s at — like maybe by six or something then we get the set list. So every city has its own reasons for that song. Maybe we’re in Detroit and we’re going to do a Motown tune. Maybe we’re in Nashville or maybe we’ll do one of their country things. You know so it depends on where we are. And Chuck Leavell is the musical director. So he’ll look at okay the last time we were in this city we did these songs so not to repeat something when we went back to Cleveland — we did that last © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
time so let’s do this one this time. So it’s kind of like, so like we do a sound check and then by six here’s the set list. Oh cool, we’re doing this.
